articleSummary: In Hanoi, Vietnam, nutrition expert Do Thi Lan warns that four summer foods are highly prone to bacterial contamination: leftover cooled rice, cut fruits (watermelon, mango, dragon fruit), processed meats such as cold cuts and sausages, and hard-boiled eggs. Processed meats can harbor Listeria, persisting even in prepared products; do not leave these out more than two hours. Refrigerate promptly, keep fridge below 4°C, reheat leftovers thoroughly, and clean fridge regularly to minimize risk.

articleSummary: Measles in the Yogyakarta Special Region (DIY) total 112 cases by early April 2026, up from about 94–96, as heightened mobility after Lebaran fuels transmission. No deaths have been reported; authorities say the outbreak remains controlled thanks to high Measles-Rubella (MR) vaccination coverage. DIY Dinas Kesehatan is accelerating immunization for children aged 9–59 months with incomplete vaccination to prevent a potential KLB (extraordinary event). Surveillance relies on the Early Warning and Rapid Response System (SKDR), evaluated weekly to detect rises in cases promptly. Measles spreads rapidly via respiratory droplets, and movement from regions with higher case counts during holidays raises risk. MR first-dose coverage exceeds 98%, second-dose around 96%, contributing to herd immunity and generally mild, outpatient cases with few hospitalizations; no fatalities reported.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Bacteria, pathogenic viruses, and antibiotic resistance genes in the coastal waters between Rimini and Riccione.
articleHeadline: Batteri, virus patogeni e geni di resistenza agli antibiotici nelle acque della costa tra Rimini e Riccione
articleSummary: Coastal waters between Rimini and Riccione in Romagna, Italy harbor pathogenic bacteria, human viruses, and antibiotic resistance genes, according to a University of Bologna study published in Scientific Reports. Using metagenomics, researchers analyzed samples from summer 2024 at urban river mouths Marecchia, Marano and Rio Melo, plus control sites away from urban inflow, in a highly urbanized, tourist-heavy stretch where summer populations exceed 800,000. Detected bacteria include Vibrio, Enterococcus, Escherichia-Shigella, and Streptococcus; viruses span Adenoviridae, Herpesviridae, and Papillomaviridae. While viral diversity is notable, infectivity and activity could not be established. Antibiotic resistance genes were identified: 99 genes across 11 antibiotic classes, many deemed critically important, potentially arising from hospitals as well as agriculture and intensive farming. The study highlights the need for genomics-based environmental monitoring to detect microbiological risks early.

articleHeadline: Pertussis resurgence after the COVID-19 pandemic in four Western Pacific Countries and the USA, highlighting the 2025 outbreak in Japan - Scientific Reports
articleSummary: Pertussis resurgence post-COVID-19 observed across Japan, Australia, New Zealand, China, and the United States, with Japan's 2025 outbreak standout. As of 2025-07-31, Japan recorded 60,826 cases (49.13/100,000), up from 4,054 in 2024. Other four countries peaked in 2024 then declined. Across all five, cases rose significantly after COVID-19 preventive measures were eased (2023-2025 vs 2020-2022; p<0.001). Japan's 2025 surge concentrated in ages 5-19, with adolescents making 56.6% of cases, predominately in non-metropolitan prefectures. The outbreak may relate to gaps in routine booster vaccination. Findings suggest re-evaluation of national immunization strategies to curb pertussis.

articleSummary: Dengue prevention in São Paulo, Brazil: With the holiday period approaching, authorities warn that about 80% of Aedes aegypti breeding sites are inside homes. articleSummary: Roche’s Xofluza (baloxavir marboxil) gains expanded age indications in China for influenza. The NMPA approved baloxavir dry suspension on 2026-03-03 for children 1 year to under 6 with uncomplicated influenza A or B, including high-risk or complicated cases. Separately, baloxavir tablets were approved on 2026-02-13 for adults and children 5 and older with uncomplicated influenza A or B, including high-risk patients. Together, these approvals extend Xofluza to 1 year and older, covering infants, children, and adults. In the DRAGONSTONE phase III trial in Chinese patients aged 1 to under 12 (both healthy and high-risk), baloxavir showed similar adverse events to oseltamivir, but with faster viral shedding cessation (24.2 hours vs 75.8 hours) and no new safety signals. WHO estimates seasonal influenza causes 30–50 million severe cases and 290,000–650,000 respiratory deaths annually; pediatric attack rates are 20–30%, rising to ~50% during peak seasons, higher than adults.

articleSummary: Thailand issues an emergency warning for Melioidosis (soil fever) after a surge in cases. From 1 January to 16 April 2026, Thailand recorded 732 melioidosis cases and 23 deaths, with the Northeast region reporting the highest incidence. Melioidosis is caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, found in soil and stagnant water, entering the body via direct contact with wounds, inhalation of contaminated dust, or drinking untreated water. Diseases range from acute high fever and shortness of breath to chronic abscesses and skin infections; severe cases can cause bacteremia and septicemia, driving mortality in the current outbreak. High-risk groups include agricultural workers and those over 50; people with diabetes, kidney disease, thalassemia, or other immunodeficiencies have higher risk of severe complications. Authorities urge protective gear (rubber boots, gloves) and prompt medical evaluation for fever >2 days or respiratory symptoms; early treatment reduces death. articleHeadline: Scientists are using mosquitoes to kill malaria causing mosquitoes - Ghana Business News
articleSummary: Malaria control researchers in Ghana and partners Target Malaria, Imperial College London and University of Oxford are pursuing gene-drive technology to suppress malaria vectors. Focus is on male Anopheles mosquitoes; female Anopheles gambiae, Anopheles coluzzii, Anopheles arabiensis, and Anopheles funestus transmit Plasmodium to humans. In Africa, malaria deaths reached about 610,000 in 2024, with roughly 95% on the continent. Gene-drive modifications are copied nearly 100% to offspring, causing generations to accumulate the trait and reducing female fertility; in laboratory cages, egg production declines and populations collapse. Field trials would involve releasing modified males but require regulatory and community engagement. The work complements existing tools (bed nets, indoor spraying, larval management). World Malaria Day is April 25; diagnostics advances like Lab-on-a-Chip Dragonfly and Lacewing support rapid detection.

Authorities reported immediate escalation of surveillance, laboratory testing, and field investigations, with 196 identified contacts all testing negative so far; no further health updates on the patients were provided. Nipah is a zoonotic virus with no approved vaccine and a high case-fatality range (40-75%). Common symptoms include high fever, vomiting, and respiratory illness; severe disease can cause seizures, encephalitis, and coma. Fruit bats are the natural hosts and the probable source of human infections. Nipah was first detected in 1998 (Malaysia); India’s first outbreak occurred in West Bengal in 2001. Large Kerala outbreaks followed in 2018 (at least 17 deaths) and in 2023 (two deaths). Indian health authorities say the situation remains under permanent surveillance and all necessary public health measures are active to prevent further spread.
